quote.text: In 2024, Akron ranked 13th among 29 US metros with at least 2,000 NAICS 326 jobs on the average weekly wage and 8th once local prices are counted, where $1,291 a week buys like $1,383 (BLS QCEW and BEA RPP).

plant.text: When you recruit from pricier metros, compare offers on what they buy: Akron’s average $1,291 a week buys like $1,383 at national-average prices.
Expect some metros to out-pay Akron even after local prices: Los Angeles pays $1,908 a week, which still buys like $1,680 against Akron’s $1,383.

claims.text: Akron ranks 13th nominal and 8th price-adjusted among 29 matched metros with at least 2,000 jobs; across all 155 matched metros it ranks 60th and 48th. At 8th, Akron's adjusted wage sits less than $6 a week from either neighboring rank.
claims.source: BLS QCEW 2024 private NAICS326 by-industry file; BEA MARPP 2024, https://apps.bea.gov/regional/zip/MARPP.zip; archive footnotes and source-level checks in test_geography_checks.py; NAICS 326; BLS QCEW and BEA RPP
claims.assert: (lambda a, big: (a['big_rank_nominal'], a['big_rank_real'], a['big_climb'], a['rank_nominal'], a['rank_real']) == (13,8,5,60,48) and 0 < big[a['big_rank_real']-2]['real'] - a['real'] < 6 and 0 < a['real'] - big[a['big_rank_real']]['real'] < 6)(one(r for r in D['big'] if r['area']=='10420'), sorted(D['big'], key=lambda r: -r['real'])) and len(D['big'])==29 and len(D['metros'])==155 and D['meta']['big_floor']==2000

Rewrite the associated sentence and correction before publication.
